forbidden.name: no-circular
forbidden.comment: Circular dependencies make modules impossible to reason about or test in isolation. Break the cycle (usually by extracting the shared piece into a lower layer).

forbidden.name: pure-logic-stays-pure
forbidden.comment: src/access and src/lib are the pure-logic floor: they must depend on nothing else in src (only types and third-party libs). If you need framework data, pass it in as a plain value. This is what keeps them unit-testable without mocks.

forbidden.name: nothing-imports-app
forbidden.comment: The Next.js app/routing layer (src/app) is the top layer: it composes everything else and nothing imports it back. Phrased as 'anything outside src/app must not import src/app' rather than enumerating the lower layers, so a NEW source directory is governed automatically without anyone remembering to add it here.

forbidden.name: not-to-unresolvable
forbidden.comment: An import that does not resolve is a broken path (a typo, a renamed file, a missing dependency). It would fail at runtime; fail it at the gate instead.

forbidden.name: not-to-dev-dep
forbidden.comment: Production source must not import a devDependency (a test util, a build tool). Those are absent from a production install, so this would crash in prod. Move the dependency, or the code.

forbidden.name: not-to-spec
forbidden.comment: Production code must never import a test/spec file.

forbidden.name: no-deprecated-core
forbidden.comment: Do not import deprecated Node.js core modules (punycode, domain, sys, the constants module, ...). They are slated for removal.
